title: Writeup error: $c_0$ defined as volume of an infinite-measure set in Prop `prop:collapse`

comments.author: human
comments.body:
In Proposition `prop:collapse` (§2.3 of solution.tex) the constant is defined as
$$c_0:=\operatorname{vol}\big((N_n\cap K)\backslash N_n(P_n\cap K)\big)>0.$$
But $N_n(P_n\cap K)\supseteq N_n$ and $N_n$ is **non-compact**, so the quotient
$(N_n\cap K)\backslash N_n(P_n\cap K)$ has **infinite Haar volume**; the claim "$c_0>0$" (a finite positive number) is ill-defined.

**What is actually true.** The integrand $g\mapsto W(\operatorname{diag}(g,1)u_Q)\,V(g)\,|\det g|^{s-1/2}$ is genuinely left-$(N_n)$-invariant (the $\psi^{-1}$ from $W$ and $\psi$ from $V$ cancel), so it descends to a function on $N_n\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n$. With the quotient Haar measure, integrating over the support $N_n\backslash N_n(P_n\cap K)\cong (N_n\cap K)\backslash(P_n\cap K)$ gives directly
$$\Psi(s,W,V)=\psi(-Q)\int_{(N_n\cap K)\backslash(P_n\cap K)}V(p)\,dp .$$
No "$N_n$-fibre volume" factor appears, contrary to the phrase "absorbing the volume of the $N_n$-fibre into the constant $c_0$."

**Fix.** Define instead $c_0:=\operatorname{vol}\big((N_n\cap K)\backslash(P_n\cap K)\big)\in(0,\infty)$ — this quotient **is** compact — or set $c_0=1$ with the natural compatible measure normalization, and state explicitly that the integrand descends to $N_n\backslash\mathrm{GL}_n$. The final conclusion ($\Psi$ is a nonzero constant) is unaffected, but the displayed definition and the measure-descent step must be corrected for the formula to be valid.
